author: thomas_hardy
text:
WHEN I DUST

_When I dust_,
The sun is low;
And with his rays
I am made hollow.

My wings are pale
As one of them might be;
Nor have they weight
Of any thing!

I will not say
That it is sad to die;
But yet, indeed,
It would be nice!

In a dry house
Without any breeze,
There’s no good place
For me! _O that there were a room in heaven
With none but me in it_;—that would be fine!

author: sara_teasdale
text:

I've eaten a licorice allsort;
My little sister took her doll;
Now you must tell me where my aunt is gone?
Aunt Fanny has returned to-night.
She walked into our kitchen door,
And with her she brought this dusty sort.

We had been watching for her long;
But now it seems that I have wrong.
For on her face was something strange,
The thing which one might call despair.

When the sun has done its work of heating up the earth it begins to cool off again. The ground loses heat more slowly than the air above it but eventually all the warmth is taken out of it. Then the atmosphere does not absorb so much heat from the land as before. As a result the temperature falls rapidly. This cooling process continues till morning comes.

As you can see night-time temperatures are usually lower than day ones even though there may be no clouds around. A blanket of cold air descends towards the surface during the night. It becomes colder still as it sinks down into warmer regions

Little God

The little god had a heart as big as itself.
It would do any good it could;
And often when its small body was tired of playing,
Or at dinner did not have to stay very long,
It went wandering in the forest to see what there might be
That needed anything from the little god.

13.

THOUGH SMILES BE SMALL.

Smile to thy neighbour; smile thou first!
And smiling take thy pleasure on.
Smile on this little earth of ours,
Though heaven above be frowning,
Smile with us in our joys or cares,
And we shall share thy happiness.
When life is bright, and all things bloom,
Why shouldst not thou rejoice?
It is enough to breathe within these walls,
To live within the circle formed
By hills that watch the valley below
Where children laugh at play.
